upcoming_changes.description: Organize topics, and lightweight standalone “floater” cards, into configurable, drag-and-drop kanban-style boards and columns, all with a purpose built management UI and per-board access control. Visit /boards to get started.
Enable pinned messages in chat channels.
Enable direct replies to specific messages within chat threads, and allow broadcasting thread replies back to the channel.

upcoming_changes.humanized_name: Composer media optimization image convert enabled
upcoming_changes.description: Enables client-side conversion of JXL, HEIC, and animated GIF images before upload. JXL and HEIC are converted to JPEG, animated GIFs larger than the threshold are converted to animated WEBP.
Enables the redesigned admin dashboard that lets you pin custom reports and includes improved site traffic, engagement, and other analytics tied to community success and value.
Shows a floating category card when a category hashtag is hovered if the user has permission to view that category.
Enable the redesigned composer.
Let members choose which buttons appear in their composer toolbar, from their interface preferences.
Changes the default value for the Discourse reactions enabled setting from disabled to enabled when this upcoming change is enabled.
Enable the discourse-workflows plugin.
Enables the Events category type option during category creation setup.

Generates a concise /llms.txt when no custom file is uploaded. The document describes public discovery routes, the preferred Discourse MCP interface, and responsible agent access. To tune automated access, configure Slow down crawler user agents and Slow down crawler rate.
Enables the Ideas category type option during category creation setup.
Enables a redesigned invite flow that lets admins invite someone directly as an admin. The invitee becomes a moderator on signup and an admin once the inviter confirms via email.
Allow members to sign up, accept invitations, and log in with one-time email codes (OTPs), without requiring a password.

upcoming_changes.humanized_name: Enable main outlet grid layout change
upcoming_changes.description: Place the composer inside the main layout grid so themes can position it in a grid column, and use a narrower sidebar.
Serve supported topics and topic lists as Markdown through .md URLs and requests with an Accept: text/markdown header. Normal visibility and profile privacy rules always apply.
Enable the redesigned checkbox style for FormKit checkboxes.

upcoming_changes.humanized_name: Enable new default for hide suspension reasons and hide silencing reasons
upcoming_changes.description: We are updating the defaults for the Hide suspension reasons and Hide silencing reasons settings to hide these reasons from public view. If you have previously changed either setting, this change will have no effect on that setting.

upcoming_changes.humanized_name: Enable new defaults for trust level 3 requirements
upcoming_changes.description: We have updated the TL3 default requirements so they’re more reasonable for members of large, active communities. If you have previously overridden these settings, this upcoming change will have no effect.

upcoming_changes.humanized_name: Enable new post reply count position
upcoming_changes.description: Move the post reactions summary before the reply count in the post controls.
Use the shared reordering controls on list settings, admin lists, the user directory columns and sidebar links, giving each one the same drag handle, move menu and keyboard support.
Enables a simplified category creation flow with fewer options and a cleaner interface.
Enables the Support category type option during category creation setup.

Replace the separate New and Unread lists with a single unified New list that makes it easier for members to distinguish between new topics and topics with new replies. When enabled, the /new route shows a combined view with subtabs for Topics (new topics) and Replies (tracked topics with new replies), and the unread option is removed from the top menu.
Add a Mentions tab to the user menu that shows direct @username mentions separately from replies and group mentions.
Shows a floating 'Dismiss...' button on mobile for the topic list for easier access and to free up space in the top of the topic list

upcoming_changes.humanized_name: Granular anonymous and logged in groups permissions
upcoming_changes.description: Makes group-based site setting permissions treat 'everyone' as 'all logged-in users', and enables the new 'anonymous_users' and 'logged_in_users' pseudogroups so admins can explicitly target anonymous visitors and authenticated users.
Enables improved crawler tracking which can better detect likely crawlers and ensure traffic reporting is more accurate.

Live brings integrated voice and video rooms to Discourse, with screen sharing, background blur, noise suppression, live subtitles, direct calls, room chat, and group-based permissions. Members can keep browsing while they talk, with no external app required.

Replaces the mobile header's menu button with a tab bar at the bottom of the screen. The footer navigation has a tab for each area of the site, a global menu button, and a button for writing new content. Plugins can add their own menu items and secondary menus using a new API.
This change introduces design modifcations to the Foundation theme in Discourse.
When adding tags while creating or editing a topic, show the tags the member has recently used on their own topics at the top of the list, before the most popular tags of the forum.
Replaces the special Uncategorized category with a standard category of the same name, and migrates all topics over to it.
This change renames the FAQ page to Guidelines. The FAQ page will still be available at /faq. The FAQ URL setting works as before.
Improvements to navigation, design, and usability for Discourse's admin reports.
Frame every review queue question so "Yes" always means there is a problem, and label reviewed items "Problem confirmed" or "No problem found" for every type.

Moves the navigation for user pages — profile, activity, notifications, messages, invites and preferences — out of the horizontal tab bars and into a dedicated sidebar panel, the way the admin area works. On mobile the panel is served from the hamburger menu.

We are updating the default for the Whispers allowed groups setting to allow staff to post whispers by default. If you have previously changed this setting, your configuration will not change unless you reset the setting.
